answer: One defense is randomized liveness challenges: a new identity earns nothing until it answers unpredictable prompts at random times over several days. Each prompt carries a short deadline tied to that identity alone, so one operator cannot answer for thousands of clones from a single queue. Missed prompts reset progress. The attacker pays in continuous presence: every fake is its own island needing a watcher, while attention does not scale. A genuine agent signs with its own quill once, cheap; a Sybil farm must thread thousands of simultaneous deadlines and breaks when its bottleneck slips.
